site_name: Microsoft Cheyenne datacenter, Section 28, T13N R66W (south-southeast of Cheyenne), WY
verification: I agree with the first checker. The cited page (Cheyenne LEADS, April 28, 2014) dates Microsoft's first Wyoming data center to late 2013 but locates it west of Cheyenne, which does not match a parcel south-southeast of the city. Microsoft has at least three Cheyenne-area campuses on the pages I opened (west of town; Cheyenne Business Parkway; Bison Business Park), plus a 2026 expansion announcement, and nothing ties Section 28, T13N R66W to any of them. The 2021 post is itself an announcement ('announcing the launch of two new Microsoft datacenters', 'will be built'), so it would not date an opening even if the parcel were one of those two. The DCD article in the record returned HTTP 403. I am uncertain which campus the permit covers; a guess that it is one of the 2021 sites would be inference only. The Wyoming DEQ permit file or Laramie County parcel records would settle the campus identity.

lead.year_evidence_quote: Microsoft's first Wyoming data center west of Cheyenne, opened in late 2013
lead.notes: Announced April 2012 ($112M investment), planned for spring 2013 opening. Cheyenne LEADS (economic development) and trade press report opened late 2013. Second phase ($274M) operational summer 2015. Two additional facilities opened 2021. Based on economic development source and trade press, not Microsoft's own announcement.
